Then we need call show_transformed_input maybe. We need ensure exactly 3 demos shown. We need infer rule.

Rule: black background 0, blue squares 1. Output same size. For every horizontal line with two blue squares separated by single space (i.e., pattern 1,0,1 at consecutive cells), fill middle with red 2. Only horizontal, not vertical. Keep blue blue, black black. So simply replace any 0 at (i,j) where (i,j-1)=1 and (i,j+1)=1 with 2. Also possible overlapping? E.g. 1,0,1,0,1 -> middle zeros both filled? Pattern 1,0,1 at positions 0,1,2 gives fill pos1. positions 2,3,4 gives fill pos3. So 1,2,1,2,1. Yes.

Verifier: x0 leastcolor(I) = 0 likely (black most common). x1 = height. vsplit(I, height) creates rows each as 1xwidth grid? vsplit grid into n=height vertical splits, each height//n =1 row. x4 = rbind(ofcolor, x0): ofcolor(piece, 0) indices of black in each row. x5 = chain(recolor 2, delta, ofcolor 0): delta of black indices within row = bounding box minus black indices. For a row, black indices. If black indices span? Let's see: delta(patch) bounding box of patch minus patch. For row of black cells. If row has black at positions e.g. 0,1,3,4 and blue at 2 => black bbox 0..4, delta {2}; recolor 2 {2}. So fills any non-black within horizontal extent of black. That's equivalent to: in each row, all positions between leftmost black and rightmost black that are not black get colored 2. Wait that includes blue squares between black cells? Let's test row [0,0,1,0,1]: black indices {0,1,3}; bbox 0..3; delta {2} (since 2 not black) -> paint red at col2. But blue at col4 outside bbox. Whereas rule says fill between two blue squares separated by single space. Row [0,0,1,0,1] has blue at 2 and 4 separated by col3 black -> fill col3 red? Wait example row1: [0,0,1,0,1] output [0,0,1,2,1]. Yes fill col3. Black indices {0,1,3}; bbox 0..3, delta {2}? Wait indices: row [0,0,1,0,1], black at 0,1,3. bbox 0..3, non-black at 2 -> recolor 2 at 2. But output has red at 3, not 2! Hmm verifier? Let's re-evaluate vsplit maybe offset? vsplit(I, x1=5) gives 5 rows of height1. x4=rbind(ofcolor, x0) where x0=leastcolor=0. ofcolor(row, 0) returns indices of 0 in the row. For row1 [0,0,1,0,1], black indices {0,1,3}. delta({0,1,3}) = backdrop = {0,1,2,3} minus patch = {2}. recolor(2, delta({0,1,3})) = {(2,(0,2))?} Actually index 2. Then paint row with red at col2. But output row1 red at col3. Contradiction. Wait leastcolor might be 1? Count 0s: row all? Input grid: row0 five 0s, row2 five 0s, row4 1,0,1,0,0 -> three 0s; 0 total? row0 5, row1 3, row2 5, row3 3, row4 3 = 19 zeros. ones: row1 2, row3 2, row4 2 =6. leastcolor = 1 (blue) because 1 appears less than 0! Ah leastcolor returns least common, so x0=1. Then ofcolor(row, 1): indices of blue in row. delta of blue indices within row: If blue at 2,4 -> bbox 2..4 minus {2,4} = {3}; recolor 2 at 3. Yes. So rule via verifier: for each row, find all blue cells, take bounding box (min to max), fill all non-blue cells within that span with red 2. That's equivalent to: any black cell horizontally between the leftmost and rightmost blue in that row becomes red. Not just single gap. If row has blue at positions 0 and 4 only, all middle black become red 2. But natural language says "every time you see two blue squares in any line with a single space in between, you fill in that space with red square Only pay attention to squares going across and not up and down." It mentions single space, but verifier generalizes to fill entire horizontal span between outermost blues. Need craft demos reflecting verifier, not just literal. We need teach student (which infers from examples). We should choose demonstrations that disambiguate full-span behavior vs single-gap. Important! The given example doesn't disambiguate much: row1 blue at 2 and4 gap single; row3 blue at 0,2 gap single; row4 same; vertical patterns not filled (rows 3,4 have 1,0,1 both rows; vertical 1 at col0 rows3,4 with single black? Actually row3 col0=1, row4 col0=1 adjacent no gap. row3 col2=1 row4 col2=1; vertical no gap). So example only single horizontal gaps. The verifier's actual behavior: fill all black between leftmost and rightmost blue in each row, regardless of gap length. We need produce demos showing this. The task says "every time you see two blue squares in any line with a single space in between, fill in that space" but verifier is more general. We must match verifier.
